$comment: Shared pre-state spec for the built-in roleplay-templates seeder differential
(P4.4u3, family 1). Drives BOTH the v4 oracle (cases/builtin-templates.ts,
which runs v4's REAL seedBuiltInTemplates) and the Rust port
(builtin_templates_equivalence). Three states exercise the three seeder paths:
- `fresh`          : empty table → INSERT both built-ins (SCHEMA-order
- `legacy-builtins`: a PRE-CODEC instance (P4.D341) — Standard + Quilltap RP
built-ins whose narration cells are planted RAW (`*`,
`["[","]"]`, as the pre-`778b97b2b` layer stored them)
and a user row with a SQL-NULL narration cell. The seeder
must rewrite both built-in cells ENCODED (`"*"`), add
the two new columns, INSERT Novel, and leave the user row
alone — the first-boot rewrite (R-6) both sides perform.
`rawNarration` / `rawNarrationNull` are post-create RAW
UPDATEs (bypassing the codec), stripped before create.
delimiters, the fresh-instance path).
- `stale-builtin`  : a built-in `Standard` with stale content → UPDATE-in-
place (proving upgrade-drift; the delimiters land in
SEED-LITERAL order, the v4 collection.updateOne quirk).
- `user-same-name` : a USER `Standard` (isBuiltIn=false) → the built-in is
INSERTED alongside it (the isBuiltIn-keying invariant).
Each pre-row is created via the real repo with a PINNED id + timestamps so both
sides start byte-identical; the seeder's minted ids/timestamps are normalized
out of the compared dump (keyed by name+isBuiltIn).
SAFETY: testPepperBase64 is the shared throwaway 32-byte key, not the real
Friday pepper.

pre.name: Standard
pre.description: A user's own template that happens to share the name.
pre.systemPrompt: User-authored prompt; must NOT be touched by the seeder.

pre.name: Novel
pre.description: A user's own Novel; the seeder keys on isBuiltIn.
